root_cause.text: The WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) in pm_restore_gfp_mask() was added under the mistaken assumption that the function is only called when GFP mask restriction is active, but hibernation code paths call it defensively even when restriction has not been applied (saved_gfp_count == 0), causing a spurious kernel warning instead of a silent no-op.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the WARN_ON wrapper from the `!saved_gfp_count` check, changing `if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count)` to `if (!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count)`. The commit message explicitly states that "Some hibernation paths call pm_restore_gfp_mask() defensively where the GFP mask may or may not be restricted" and that before the refactoring this was a silent no-op.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary WARN_ON check in pm_restore_gfp_mask when saved_gfp_count is zero.
intent_record.what: Replaced `WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count)` with a simple `!saved_gfp_count` check in the condition of the `if` statement in `pm_restore_gfp_mask`.
intent_record.how: The function no longer triggers a kernel warning when `saved_gfp_count` is zero at the start of the call; the behavior otherwise remains identical (returns early if count is zero or becomes zero after decrement).
